key_insight: This paper investigates whether dense, token-by-token teacher guidance helps a smaller model reach a target accuracy with less training compute than GRPO reinforcement learning. The supplied abstract is truncated, so it does not establish which approach wins.
problem_solved: Determine whether on-policy distillation offers a genuine compute-efficiency advantage over GRPO, and how that comparison changes with task difficulty, model size, domain, and optimization choices.
method: Compare vanilla reverse-KL on-policy distillation with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO).
Train the distillation student on its own generated rollouts, using per-token supervision from a frozen teacher.
Measure held-out accuracy against training FLOPs across task difficulties, student–teacher sizes, domains, and optimization settings.
impact: The comparison helps practitioners evaluate teacher-guided distillation versus reinforcement learning under a training-compute budget. Specific recommendations require the full results, which are absent from the provided excerpt.
visual_elements: Side-by-side training pipelines: student rollouts with frozen-teacher token guidance versus GRPO reinforcement learning.

paper_title: Unpacking the Compute Efficiency of Strong-to-Weak OPD against GRPO
paper_authors: Zeyu Leo Liu, Yang Li, Bo Pang, Emre Can Acikgoz, Xuan-Phi Nguyen
